This Application coming on for orders upon perusing the application and upon hearing the arguments of M/S.S.RAJEEV, V.VINAY, M.S.ANEER, SARATH K.P., PRERITH PHILIP JOSEPH, ANILKUMAR C.R., K.S.KIRAN KRISHNAN, Advocates for the petitioner and of the PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the respondent,the court passed the following:

 P.G. AJITHKUMAR, J.
 -----------------------------------------------------------
 Crl.M.A.No.1 of 2023  in  Crl.Appeal No.1451 of 2023  -----------------------------------------------------------
 Dated this the 12th day of June, 2024  ORDER
This is a petition filed by the appellant under Section 389(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Code).

The petitioner would contend that he is innocent and there is every chance for allowing the Ali vs State Of Kerala on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193872847/
1 appeal and acquitting him.
He was on bail during the trial of the case.
In such circumstances, he claims that he is entitled to get execution of his sentence suspended.
2. The learned Public Prosecutor filed an objection on behalf of the respondent.
It is contended that the evidence adduced by the prosecution proved beyond doubt that the petitioner had committed the offence alleged against him.
The offence proved against the petitioner is grievous.
On account of the offence he has committed and the consequent ostracisation, the victim girl, who was aged only 12 years at the time of occurrence, has been put to untold miseries.
Crl.M.A.No.1 of 2023 in Considering the gravity and nature of the offence and the tenure of the sentence imposed
, the petitioner is not entitled to get an order to suspend the sentence.

3. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned Public Prosecutor.
4.

The petitioner was convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 354, 376(2)(j), 341 and 509 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and under Section 6 r/w 5(m) and Section 10 r/w 9(l) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The term of sentence the petitioner has to undergo is imprisonment for 10 years.

5. The case of the prosecution was as follows:
The petitioner is a neighbour of the victim girl.
She went to the house of the petitioner for giving him a card as instructed from her house.
The petitioner forcibly took the victim to his bedroom, hugged her and subjected her to penetrative sexual assault by fingering.
Later on several occasions the petitioner offering sweets, had taken the victim to his house and sexually assaulted.

Lastly, on a day in August, 2019 while she Crl.M.A.No.1 of 2023 in was returning home after her tuition classes, she was wrongly restrained at the pathway and sexually assaulted her by pressing at her breast and vagina.
The trial court believing the evidence tendered by the prosecution found the petitioner guilty as mentioned above.
6. The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that there have been serious discrepancies in the evidence of the victim and the delay in lodging the complaint.
Therefore, the conviction is based on unreliable and insufficient evidence, and the appeal will be allowed.
Having gone through the judgment and considered the available materials, prima facie, I am unable to agree with the contention that the findings leading to the conviction of the petitioner is wrong.
7. As pointed out by the learned Public Prosecutor the offence the petitioner has committed is serious in nature as a child of 12 years was subjected to sexual violence by an elderly person.
The petitioner was convicted and sentenced on 14.09.2023.
He has been in jail since the said date.
He was in jail for two months during the period of investigation also.

Considering that the petitioner has been under detention for a considerable period, his age and also his clear antecedents, he can be granted bail by suspending execution of the sentence, subject to conditions.

This is a petition filed by the appellant under Section 389(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Code).
He was on bail during the trial of the case.
, the petitioner is not entitled to get an order to suspend the sentence.
The petitioner was convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 354, 376(2)(j), 341 and 509 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and under Section 6 r/w 5(m) and Section 10 r/w 9(l) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.
opennyai_summary.arguments: It is contended that the evidence adduced by the prosecution proved beyond doubt that the petitioner had committed the offence alleged against him.
opennyai_summary.decision:
The offence proved against the petitioner is grievous.
The petitioner was convicted and sentenced on 14.09.2023.
He was in jail for two months during the period of investigation also.
Considering that the petitioner has been under detention for a considerable period, his age and also his clear antecedents, he can be granted bail by suspending execution of the sentence, subject to conditions.
Accordingly, this petition is allowed and the petitioner is granted bail on his executing a bond for Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees one lakh only), with two solvent sureties for the like amount each, to the satisfaction of the trial court, subject to the following conditions:
i) The petitioner shall deposit entire fine amount in the trial court within one month;
ii) He shall not enter the local limits of Aluva West Police Station till the final disposal of this appeal;
iii) During the bail period, he shall not get involved in any offence; and iv) He shall not contact or try to intimidate the victim or witnesses examined in the case.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to apply before this Court for cancellation of the suspension of sentence.
